title: The canonical base-change components commute with both relative restriction maps
statement: Let g′:X′→X, f′:X′→S′, f:X→S and g:S′→S form a cartesian square of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-base-change]. Let K∈D(O_X), K′∈D(O_X′), and φ:L(g′)K→K′ [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-pullback]. Let U,V be arbitrary opens of X, with no compactness, covering or quasi-coherence assumption. Use the canonical unit and difference maps and the local arrows αW and global arrow αX of [def-pc-relative-mv-maps]. Then the square between the source and target unit maps, with vertical components αX and αU⊕αV, commutes. The square between the source and target difference maps, with vertical components αU⊕αV and α(U∩V), also commutes. This asserts no distinguishedness or boundary compatibility.

source.place: Tags 08BV (lemma-unbounded-mayer-vietoris), 08HZ (lemma-unbounded-relative-mayer-vietoris), and 08HY (remark-base-change); perfect.tex, Tag 0DJ9 (lemma-single-complex-base-change), induction diagram

proof.text: For the first square, apply biproduct projection extensionality. The U and V projections are precisely the single-open unit squares.

For the second square, apply biproduct injection extensionality. Use the single-inclusion restriction square for U∩V⊆U. For the V injection, negate the square for U∩V⊆V and use additivity of composition. The defining Mayer–Vietoris difference signs agree.

lean.statement:
theorem relativeMV_restriction_squares
    [∀ Z : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))]
    {X S X' S' : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (f' : X' ⟶ S') (g : S' ⟶ S) (g' : X' ⟶ X)
    (hpull : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (K : schemeDerivedCategory X) (K' : schemeDerivedCategory X')
    (φ : (derivedPullback g').obj K ⟶ K')
    (U V : X.Opens) :
    let a := relativeMVLocalArrow f f' g g' hpull K K' φ
    let aX := relativeMVGlobalArrow f f' g g' hpull K K' φ
    relativeMVSourceFirst f g U V K ≫ biprod.map (a U).hom (a V).hom =
      aX.hom ≫ relativeMVTargetFirst g' f' U V K' ∧
    relativeMVSourceSecond f g U V K ≫ (a (U ⊓ V)).hom =
      biprod.map (a U).hom (a V).hom ≫ relativeMVTargetSecond g' f' U V K'
